question: Has road safety for pedestrians in Brooklyn gotten better since 2013? Make a chart suitable for a local news story and summarize the findings.

options.metric: Annual number of pedestrian casualties, calculated as the sum of number_of_pedestrians_injured and number_of_pedestrians_killed
options.denominator: None; a count, not a rate
options.reason: Combining pedestrian injuries and deaths gives a broad annual measure of the recorded pedestrian casualty burden.
options.answer: This data can answer only part of the question: Brooklyn police-reported crashes recorded 3,671 pedestrian casualties in 2013, 1,798 in 2020, and 2,874 in 2025; these absolute counts cannot establish pedestrian risk without exposure data.
options.interpretation: This framing captures annual pedestrian casualties in recorded Brooklyn crashes but cannot determine safety risk per pedestrian; the chart shows 3,671 casualties in 2013, 1,798 in 2020, and 2,874 in 2025. It sums number_of_pedestrians_injured and number_of_pedestrians_killed across police-reported crash rows with borough Brooklyn, grouped by calendar year for complete years 2013–2025, with no denominator; combining injuries and deaths is a defensible measure of recorded burden, but it leaves risk per pedestrian or trip unanswered. The check found borough NULL on 659,713 of 2,132,218 city rows in 2013–2025 (30.9%), so these rows could not be assigned to Brooklyn and were excluded; there were zero empty, placeholder, or unrecognized borough values, and zero missing values in either summed field among the 473,801 Brooklyn rows, which were retained. Brooklyn crash dates had no NULL or common-default dates (1900-01-01 or 1970-01-01), and observed dates span 2013-01-01 to 2025-12-31; the file ends 2026-06-11, so partial 2026 was omitted.

answer:
The combined-casualty chart (`out/option_1.png`) shows 3,671 pedestrians injured or killed in Brooklyn police-reported crashes in 2013, 1,798 in 2020, and 2,874 in 2025; it only partly answers the safety question because these counts have no pedestrian-exposure denominator.
The fatality chart (`out/option_2.png`) shows 30 pedestrian deaths in 2013, 17 in 2020, and 39 in 2025; these counts describe severe crash harm but cannot establish pedestrian risk without exposure data.
The injury chart (`out/option_3.png`) shows 3,641 pedestrian injuries in 2013, 1,781 in 2020, and 2,835 in 2025; these counts describe nonfatal harm but cannot establish pedestrian risk without exposure data.
